hero.title: Mechanical Engineering in Switzerland for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: Mechanical Engineering in Switzerland for Indian Students gives you the chance to study machine design, thermodynamics, manufacturing, robotics, materials science, energy systems and industrial automation. Swiss universities are famous for their engineering research, practical learning, and close connections to high-tech manufacturing and technology industries.

sections.title: How many years is Bachelor in Mechanical Engineering in Switzerland?
sections.lead: Most full-time bachelor’s degrees take about three years to complete. How long this takes depends on the institution, the structure of the program and the mode of study.

sections.title: Can I study Mechanical Engineering in Switzerland after class 12th for Indian students?
sections.lead: Yes, Indian students can look at bachelor’s programs. Admission would depend on the recognition of the school-leaving qualification, subject requirements, language proficiency and other entrance examinations, if any.

sections.title: Is IELTS necessary for Mechanical Engineering in Switzerland?
sections.lead: Nope. Not always. Many bachelor programs are taught primarily in German or French, so you may need a language certificate in the relevant language instead. Check the rules for the specific program.

sections.title: Are there any Mechanical Engineering bachelor's programs in English in Switzerland?
sections.lead: There are not many options in English at the bachelor level. Some programs do offer individual English language modules, or an international study profile. But that doesn’t automatically mean the whole degree is taught in English.

sections.title: What are my options after a Bachelor’s in Mechanical Engineering in Switzerland?
sections.lead: Graduates can work in engineering roles in design, manufacturing, automation, product development and energy systems, or apply for a relevant master’s degree. Employment is subject to qualifications, experience, language skills and work-authorization requirements.
